A 85-year-old white male presents for evaluation of abnormal liver function tests. His medical history
includes well-controlled hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide. He reports moderate alcohol
consumption (2-3 drinks weekly), denies smoking and illicit drug use, and lives with his wife. Physical
examination reveals a BMI of 33 with normal vital signs and no evidence of acute or chronic liver
disease. Laboratory results show: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | | Aspartate
aminotransferase (U/liter) | 45 | 0–35 | | Alanine aminotransferase (U/liter) | 65 | 0–35 | | Alkaline
phosphatase (U/liter) | 90 | 30–120 | | Direct bilirubin (mg/dL) | 0.3 | 0.1–0.3 | | Total bilirubin (mg/dL) |
0.9 | 0.3–1.0 | | Prothrombin time (sec) | 12.0 | 11.1–13.1 | | Albumin (g/dL) | 4.5 | 3.5–5.5 | | Glucose
(mg/dL) | 115 | 70–100 | | Total cholesterol (mg/dL) | 260 | 125–200 | | LDL cholesterol (mg/dL) | 170 |
<130 | | HDL cholesterol (mg/dL) | 30 | ≥40 | | Triglycerides (mg/dL) | 300 | <150 | Complete blood count
and serum creatinine are normal. Hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibodies are negative.
What is the most appropriate next diagnostic test? Answer Choices: (A) Liver biopsy (B) Alpha-1
antitrypsin level and phenotype (C) Serum copper and 24-hour urinary copper (D) Anti-smooth muscle
antibodies and IgG levels (E) HFE gene mutation analysis (F) Antinuclear antibodies and anti-liver
kidney microsomal antibodies (G) Antimitochondrial antibodies (H) Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler
flow studies (I) Serum ferritin and transferrin saturation (J) Ceruloplasmin level
 A. Antinuclear antibodies and anti-liver kidney microsomal antibodies
B. Anti-smooth muscle antibodies and IgG levels
C. Antimitochondrial antibodies
D. HFE gene mutation analysis
E. Serum copper and 24-hour urinary copper
F. Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler flow studies
G. Alpha-1 antitrypsin level and phenotype
H. Ceruloplasmin level
I. Liver biopsy
J. Serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
